editorial.description_en: Cedar board burned to preserve it. Dark and warm, and the only colour in this group whose warmth survives at low lightness.
editorial.description_ja: 焼いた杉板のような、暗くあたたかい色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.352, C 0.016, h 58.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 焼き (yaki, burning) + 杉 (sugi, cedar). Also an existing term for the board-charring technique; used here as a colour name and not as a claim about any board. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Charred Cedar" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 焼杉. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — yoru-gami at ΔE00 11.7, tetsu-suna at ΔE00 12.7, soko-zumi at ΔE00 14.2. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.016 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
